What the referee says on the stand

A stand has its own short language. When ready, the shooter gives the call, usually “Pull!” or “Ready!”. In Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ the referee passes the call to the trapper with a sound signal. The target must leave within 3 seconds of that signal; a later target is a No Bird. In Compak® Sporting a manual release must also come within 3 seconds of the call. A voice-activated release (sonopull: a microphone that launches the target when it hears your call) has a fixed delay of half a second.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 5 · Calling for the target and the 3-second release

Before anyone shoots, the referee decides when guns may be loaded and closed. The rules allow loading only on the stand, with the gun pointing down the range, once the referee has said shooting may start. While targets are being shown (presentation), and whenever shooting stops, guns are open and empty. They are closed again only when the referee allows it. In Compak® Sporting the referee starts the round with “Start” or “Competition”.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 8 · When and how to load

After each target there are only three results in the rulebook: “one” (hit), “zero” (lost) and “No Bird” (the target does not count and is thrown again). On the ground you will also hear “dead” or “good” for a hit and “lost” for a miss; some referees say nothing after a hit. In Compak® Sporting the referee announces each zero aloud or with a sound signal, so a shooter who disagrees can protest at once.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 4 · Glossary of basic terms

The shooter has a formal word too. To disagree with a decision, raise a hand at once, on the stand, and say “Protest!” or “Appeal!” (Chapter 9 · How to protest on the stand, Chapter 19 · How to protest a referee's call). More phrases a shooter needs: Phrases a shooter needs on the stand.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 9 · How to protest on the stand

Key points

  • The shooter calls “Pull!” or “Ready!”; the target must come within 3 seconds
  • Load only on the stand and only when the referee allows it; guns open during viewing and stops
  • Rule words: one = hit, zero = lost, No Bird = thrown again
  • Compak® Sporting: each zero is announced aloud or by a sound signal
  • Protest = raised hand + “Protest!” or “Appeal!”
Stand Talk

  • Referee You may load.

    Meaning: The referee allows shooting to start: put cartridges in now, gun pointing down the range.

  • Referee No bird!

    Meaning: That target does not count; do not shoot at it. It will be thrown again.

  • Referee Lost.

    Meaning: The referee scored the target as a miss (zero).

  • Referee Dead. / Good.

    Meaning: The target is a hit (one).

  • Referee Guns open, please — we’re showing the targets.

    Meaning: Everyone opens and unloads; the referee will throw the targets for viewing.

  • Referee Start. / Competition.

    Meaning: Compak® Sporting: viewing is over, the round counts from now.

For the interpreter
  • Keep these calls short and the same each time. Agree with your shooter before the round which words you will use. Add nothing of your own between the call and the shot.

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. In Sporting™ the target leaves five seconds after the referee’s signal. What is the referee’s decision?

    1. It counts as normal
    2. No Bird
    3. Zero, because the shooter called too early
    4. A warning for the trapper only
    Answer

    No Bird

    A target must leave within three seconds of the referee’s signal; a target released later is a No Bird and is thrown again.

    Chapter 5 · Calling for the target and the 3-second release

  2. In competition, when may a shooter load the gun?

    1. While walking to the next stand
    2. Behind the stand, while waiting
    3. On the stand, after the referee allows it
    4. As soon as the coach says so
    Answer

    On the stand, after the referee allows it

    Loading is allowed only on the stand, gun pointing down the range, and only once the referee has said shooting may start.

    Chapter 8 · When and how to load

  3. Which words start a formal protest on the stand?

    1. “Protest!”, with a raised hand
    2. “No Bird!”, with a raised hand
    3. “Referee, look at that target!”
    4. “Wait!”, after the next target
    Answer

    “Protest!”, with a raised hand

    Both rulebooks name “protest” or “appeal” with a raised hand, at once; “No Bird” is the referee’s word.

    Chapter 9 · How to protest on the stand
